newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-AMR to buy Brazil jets in $1 bln order.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-AMR to buy Brazil jets in $1 bln order.

text.p: U.S. airline AMR Corp's domestic carrier American Eagle announced a billion dollar order for up to 67 short-range passenger jets from Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer on Tuesday.
It said it was buying 42 of Embraers 50-seat EMB-145 regional jets and taking options on a further 25 aircraft. The firm orders alone are worth $700 million.
The two companies announced the deal at a joint news conference at the Paris air show.
An American official also said it would be announcing a further order at the show later in the day with Embraer's rival Bombardier of Canada.

The twin-engined Embraer aircraft will be powered by AE 3007A1 engines made by Allison Engine Co, the U.S. subsidiary of British aero-engine manufacturer Rolls-Royce Plc. Allison said that the order was worth in excess of $275 million.
American Eagle senior vice president Peter Pappas told the news conference that American made the decision to buy the new fleet following a succesful rationalisation of its operations last year.
The new fleet would provide additional capacity and allow the airline to replace some of its turboprop aircraft.

"American Eagle is entering a new phase," he told reporters. "At the present time these aircraft will be growth aircraft but over time we will be replacing some of our turboprops ... depending on demand in the marketplace," he said.
